# Overview

This lab uses RNA-seq data to identify differentially expressed genes and examine biological pathways using DESeq2, KEGG, Gene Ontology, and Reactome.

# Section 1. Differential Expression Analysis

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Load DESeq2
library(DESeq2)

# Load metadata and count files
metaFile <- "GSE37704_metadata.csv"
countFile <- "GSE37704_featurecounts.csv"

# Import metadata
colData <- read.csv(metaFile, row.names=1)
head(colData)

# Import count data
countData <- read.csv(countFile, row.names=1)
head(countData)
```

>**Q1.** Complete the code below to remove the troublesome first column from `countData`.

```{r}
# Remove the extra length column
countData <- as.matrix(countData[, -1])

# View updated count data
head(countData)
```

>**Q2.** Complete the code below to filter `countData` to exclude genes (rows) with 0 read counts across all samples (columns).

```{r}
# Remove genes with zero counts across all samples
countData <- countData[rowSums(countData) > 0, ]

# View filtered count data
head(countData)
```

## Running DESeq2

```{r}
# Create the DESeq2 dataset
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = countData,
  colData = colData,
  design = ~condition
)

# Run DESeq2 analysis
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# View results
dds
```

## DESeq2 Results

```{r}
# Get differential expression results
res <- results(dds)

# View results
head(res)
```

**Q3.** Call the `summary()` function on your results to see how many genes are upregulated and downregulated at the default adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.1.

```{r}
summary(res)
```

## Volcano Plot

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Create a basic volcano plot
ggplot(as.data.frame(res)) +
  aes(x = log2FoldChange,
      y = -log10(padj)) +
  geom_point()
```

>**Q4.** Improve the volcano plot by adding color, axis labels, and cutoff lines.

```{r}
# Make a color vector for all genes
mycols <- rep("gray", nrow(res))

# Color blue the genes with fold change above 2
mycols[!is.na(res$log2FoldChange) &
       abs(res$log2FoldChange) > 2] <- "blue"

# Color gray genes with adjusted p-value above 0.01
mycols[!is.na(res$padj) & res$padj > 0.01] <- "gray"

# Create improved volcano plot
ggplot(as.data.frame(res)) +
  aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj)) +
  geom_point(color = mycols, na.rm = TRUE) +
  xlab("Log2(FoldChange)") +
  ylab("-Log(P-value)") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-2, 2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.01))
```

## Adding Gene Annotation

**Q5.** Use the `mapIds()` function to add SYMBOL, ENTREZID, and GENENAME annotations to the results.

```{r}
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# View available annotation columns
columns(org.Hs.eg.db)

# Add gene symbols
res$symbol <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                     keys = row.names(res),
                     keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                     column = "SYMBOL",
                     multiVals = "first")

# Add Entrez IDs
res$entrez <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                     keys = row.names(res),
                     keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                     column = "ENTREZID",
                     multiVals = "first")

# Add gene names
res$name <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                   keys = row.names(res),
                   keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                   column = "GENENAME",
                   multiVals = "first")

# View annotated results
head(res, 10)
```

>**Q6.** Reorder the results by adjusted p-value and save them to a CSV file in your current project directory.

```{r}
# Sort results by adjusted p-value
res <- res[order(res$padj), ]

# Save results as a CSV file
write.csv(as.data.frame(res), file = "deseq_results.csv")

# View sorted results
head(res)
```

## KEGG Pathways

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(pathview)
library(gage)
library(gageData)

# Load KEGG pathway datasets
data(kegg.sets.hs)
data(sigmet.idx.hs)

# Focus on signaling and metabolic pathways
kegg.sets.hs <- kegg.sets.hs[sigmet.idx.hs]

# View the first three pathways
head(kegg.sets.hs, 3)
```

## KEGG Pathway Enrichment Analysis

```{r}
# Get log2 fold changes
foldchanges <- res$log2FoldChange

# Assign Entrez gene IDs
names(foldchanges) <- res$entrez

# View the first few fold changes
head(foldchanges)
```

## Running GAGE Pathway Analysis

```{r}
# Run KEGG pathway analysis
keggres <- gage(foldchanges, gsets = kegg.sets.hs)

# View the structure of the results
attributes(keggres)

# View the top downregulated pathways
head(keggres$less)
```

## KEGG Pathway Visualization

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: "hide"

# Generate a pathway diagram for the cell cycle
pathview(gene.data = foldchanges,
         pathway.id = "hsa04110")

# Generate a PDF-style pathway diagram
pathview(gene.data = foldchanges,
         pathway.id = "hsa04110",
         kegg.native = FALSE)
```

## Top 5 Upregulated KEGG Pathways

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Get the top 5 upregulated pathways
keggrespathways <- rownames(keggres$greater)[1:5]

# Extract the KEGG pathway IDs
keggresids <- substr(keggrespathways, start = 1, stop = 8)

# View pathway IDs
keggresids

# Generate pathway diagrams
pathview(gene.data = foldchanges,
         pathway.id = keggresids,
         species = "hsa")
```

>**Q7.** Can you do the same procedure as above to plot the pathview figures for the top 5 down-regulated pathways?

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Get the top 5 downregulated pathways
downpathways <- rownames(keggres$less)[1:5]

# Extract the KEGG pathway IDs
downids <- substr(downpathways, start = 1, stop = 8)

# View pathway IDs
downids

# Generate pathway diagrams
pathview(gene.data = foldchanges,
         pathway.id = downids,
         species = "hsa")
```

### Top 5 Downregulated KEGG Pathways

The following figures show the top five downregulated KEGG pathways.

# Section 3. Gene Ontology (GO)

## Biological Process Analysis

```{r}
# Load Gene Ontology datasets
data(go.sets.hs)
data(go.subs.hs)

# Focus on Biological Process (BP)
gobpsets <- go.sets.hs[go.subs.hs$BP]

# Run GO pathway analysis
gobpres <- gage(foldchanges, gsets = gobpsets)

# View the results
lapply(gobpres, head)
```

# Section 4. Reactome Analysis

## Significant Genes

```{r}
# Select significant genes with adjusted p-value <= 0.05
sig_genes <- res[res$padj <= 0.05 & !is.na(res$padj), "symbol"]

# Count significant genes
print(paste("Total number of significant genes:", length(sig_genes)))

# Save significant genes to a text file
write.table(sig_genes,
            file = "significant_genes.txt",
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE)
```

>**Q8.** What pathway has the most significant "Entities p-value"? Do the most significant pathways listed match your previous KEGG results? What factors could cause differences between the two methods?

**Answer:** The most significant pathway was Cell Cycle, Mitotic, with an Entities p-value of 1.48 × 10⁻⁵. This matches my KEGG results since Cell Cycle was also one of the top downregulated pathways. Some differences could be because KEGG and Reactome use different pathway databases and group genes differently.
